items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S10201

SPONSOR: CLEARE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to the powers of the
head of the office of mental health and the head of the office for
people with developmental disabilities to promulgate rules regarding
communications needs of non-English speaking individuals

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to increase access to services and support
for non-English speaking individuals.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill would amend current mental hygiene law by requiring the
commissioner of the Office of Mental Health (OMB) and the Office for
People with Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD) to provide language
limited to documents, forms, and materials being made available in the
twelve most common non-English languages in the state of New York, as
determined by United States census data.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The OMH and the OPWDD provide valuable services to individuals with a
mental health diagnosis or with a developmental disability. These
services were implemented with the intention of serving all New Yorkers.
However, without providing materials in the twelve most common non-En-
glis languages in the state, there will be barriers to treatment and
supports to those who are not proficient in the English language. This
bill would increase access to services and supports provided by the OMB
and OPWDD by requiring the commissioner of the office of mental health
and the office for people with developmental disabilities to provide
language assistance services for non-English individuals, including but
not limited to documents, forms, and materials being made available in
the twelve most common non-English languages in the state of New York,
as determined by United States census data.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect Immediately.

summary: Relates to the powers of the head of the office of mental health and the head of the office for people with developmental disabilities to promulgate rules regarding communications needs of non-English speakers seeking or receiving services; includes the provision of language services and documents in English and the twelve most common non-English languages spoken by individuals in New York State based on United States census data.
